paragraphs: In the morning, review audit findings and customer complaints and prioritize defect categories. At midday, align corrective actions with production lines and revise system documents. In the afternoon, review quality dashboards and identify yield deviations. In weekly meetings, compare system effectiveness against customer requirements. At month-end, consolidate risks and improvements for management review.

In one sentence: keep the quality system stable. The work includes building systems, organizing audits, analyzing defects, driving corrective action, monitoring yield, and maintaining compliance. It combines analysis with influence and leads quality outcomes.
